subject.title: [Bug/Docs]: local+hybrid memory_search quality can appear unstable due to extraPaths path drift + benchmark-file contamination

question: Should OpenClaw add a public memorySearch exclusion/path-hygiene contract now, and should it ship as builtin-only first or require QMD, status-diagnostic, and docs parity before merge?
rationale: The issue cannot be safely closed or auto-fixed as a narrow bug because it asks for a new config surface and changes which files enter durable recall context, while repository policy treats memory/session-state and config/default changes as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
options.body: Repair and land the open excludePaths PR with merged default/per-agent semantics, index-identity coverage, and explicit builtin-only docs while tracking QMD and diagnostics separately.

options.title: Require cross-backend contract
options.body: Pause the open PR until builtin indexing, QMD collections, watcher behavior, status diagnostics, and docs share one exclusion/path-hygiene model.

options.title: Docs and diagnostics only
options.body: Defer public exclusion config for now and improve memory status plus docs guidance around extraPaths drift, broad corpora, and benchmark contamination.

recommendation.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
recommendation.body: Repair and land the open excludePaths PR with merged default/per-agent semantics, index-identity coverage, and explicit builtin-only docs while tracking QMD and diagnostics separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The current memory host SDK and memory-core manager/status boundaries were largely shaped by steipete's recent refactors, making him the best routing candidate for the config/runtime boundary decision.
